title: Honest Interval Length for Local Effects under Weak Heterogeneous Judge Compliance
banked_reason: D-0.5 NO-PASS after three revisions: exact knowledge of latent-stratum potential-outcome means is an oracle restriction imposed precisely to delete the baseline tangent directions; no realistic design or data source establishes those means or the stipulated calibration rate.
gap_reasons: Exact knowledge of latent-stratum potential-outcome means is an oracle restriction imposed precisely to delete the baseline tangent directions; its justification gives no realistic design or data source under which those latent means are known or estimable at the stipulated rate.
proof_attempt_summary: Three D-0.5 versions retained the exact known-baseline four-score oracle experiment. The third added a conditional estimated-baseline stability theorem and repaired the fixed M=21/20 positivity linkage, but the reviewer still found no observable source for the latent baselines or the required calibration rate. The proposal never reached D0 or Lean formalization; a separately scoped unknown-baseline experiment would be needed to revisit the practical claim.
tldr: Weak and heterogeneous judge compliance leaves a bounded causal effect nonregular in an exact randomized binary oracle model with known one-half latent-stratum means and admissible rows \(n\ge\lceil(8M/3)^{2}\rceil\). The fixed type masses and known outcome means determine the treatment and outcome score centers, respectively, while the known outcome means remove additional baseline tangent directions and permit reduction of the complete joint cells to four independent Gaussian coordinates. Honest connected intervals for the predeclared quadratic-strength-weighted effect then form a compact minimax game whose certified optimizer and active heterogeneous nuisance fibers are the field-grade kernel. On \([1,21/20]\), an explicit two-null fiber family certifies a strictly positive scalar-oracle penalty and the optimized value is more than \(0.062\) shorter than the same-target Gaussian-ellipsoid projection benchmark. The oracle value transfers to exact records, while an explicit total-variation stability theorem gives \(O(\delta_{B,n})\) risk and length perturbations for externally estimated score centers; unrestricted unknown baselines remain outside scope.
gap: Evans, Hansen, and Stark solve restricted scalar location games, Schafer and Stark give general numerical expected-size machinery, and Andrews and Mikusheva formulate optimal weak-GMM decisions. None characterizes the connected-interval value generated by nonlinear target fibers in two unknown compliance strengths and two heterogeneous effects, locates its least-favorable nuisance support, or transfers that exact value to admissible original binary records in the specified known-baseline experiment.
fill: Within that oracle scope, the project derives the four sufficient Gaussian scores, proves minimax saddle and admissible-row exact-record transfer theorems, constructs convergent rational primal and dual bounds, certifies a positive heterogeneous penalty on the full box \([1,21/20]\), and proves strict improvement over a standard same-target projection interval. A separate local stability theorem bounds the value and honest-length effect of externally estimated score centers by an explicit multiple of their local-scale sup-norm error.
